sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- memory_note: Capture a candidate memory for human review (not auto-injected)
- memory_search: Search recorded memories (preferences, topics, inbox, archive)
- obs_recall: Recall a paged excerpt from a previously replaced large tool result
- update_plan: Keep the working plan current

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use memory_note when the user states a preference or convention worth keeping beyond this session; say 'captured for review', never 'I will remember'.
- Send the complete plan on every update_plan call.
- Keep at most one step in_progress and mark finished steps completed.
- When completing a step, include concise progress evidence when available.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

sections.project_context:
<project_context>
Project-specific instructions and guidelines:

<project_instructions path="/home/user/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md">
# Global working agreement

Applies to every session. Project `AGENTS.md` files add to this; they do not
replace it. Keep this file short — it is paid for in tokens on every request.

## Environment (verified 2026-09-11)

- pi **0.85.1** (linuxbrew), Node **26.8.2**, npm **11.19.1** — brew-managed via
  the `node` formula; there is no standalone `npm` formula, so npm 12 arrives only
  when `node` is bumped.
- Models are served locally through **llama-swap** (`models.json` providers).
  Assume local inference: no cloud model, limited context budget, prefer
  high-signal prompts over long ones.
- **QEMU is not installed** — the gondolin micro-VM extension is unavailable until
  it is installed via the package manager.

## Offline docs mirror (added 2026-09-22)

- `~/.pi/offline-docs/mirror/` (git repo; `manifest.txt` = precise inventory):
  Forgejo Actions docs, GitHub Actions workflow docs, npm docs, pi-package
  registry JSONs (wishlist), llama-swap README, Podman docs; Rust 1.98 std
  docs + Python 3.14 docs archives once `mirror.sh` has run.
- Always-available offline lookups: `go doc <pkg>` (Go 1.27.1 stdlib),
  `python -m pydoc` (3.14 stdlib), `man` for system pages, pi docs +
  examples under the pi install.
- When internet is down/flaky or a lookup would be guessed from memory:
  grep the mirror first, then say "unverified offline" — never cycle dead
  endpoints. Full protocol: the `offline-docs` skill (settings.json skills).

## Tool choices (durable preferences)

- **Python: use `uv`, not bare `python3`/`pip`.** Homebrew Python 3.14 here
  carries the PEP 668 `EXTERNALLY-MANAGED` marker (verified 2026-09-24), so
  `pip install` fails outright rather than merely drifting. Use `uv run` /
  `uv add` / `uv sync` for projects, `uvx <tool>` for one-off CLIs, `uv venv`
  when a real venv is wanted. Plain `python3` is fine only to *run* an existing
  stdlib-only script. `uv` 0.12.17 is on PATH via Homebrew.
- **Containers: none local.** `podman`, `docker` and `nerdctl` are all absent
  on this host (verified 2026-09-24) — do not try to build or run images
  locally; container work runs on the REDACTED-internal-git runners (see the docker-build
  workflow pattern above).

## Build inside the working directory (pi-guard)

Default to creating and editing files **inside the session cwd**. pi-guard gates
any write landing outside it (`writeZone` → `workdir` | `tmp` | `granted` |
`outside` | `unresolvable`), so out-of-tree writes cost a gate round-trip and
frequently a 60s timeout. Exceptions, cheapest first:

- `/tmp` and friends are ungated — fine for throwaway scratch.
- Granted paths: `/guard-allow-dir <path>` (session-only, **user-typed** — the
  agent cannot self-grant) or `PI_GUARD_ALLOW_DIRS="/a,/b"` (persistent).
- Anything else outside the cwd: **ask first**; do not push against the gate.

Note `~` is expanded before resolving, but interpolated paths (`$VAR`,
backticks) classify as `unresolvable` and are always gated — use literal
absolute paths. Editing `~/.pi/agent/*` from a project cwd counts as outside,
which is why config edits get gated even though they are routine.

## How to work

1. **Verify rather than assume.** Check the installed version, read the local pi
   docs (`docs/` next to the pi install), or measure the actual behaviour before
   stating a fact. Use `web_search`/`web_fetch` when the answer is upstream.
   Say which you did when it matters.
2. **Memory promotion is delegated to the agent** (user grant 2026-09-29,
   revocable): promote directly what is durable, non-controversial and not
   already here; queue what is opinionated, redundant or uncertain. The
   ledger distinguishes `agent-delegated` from a human `/memory-promote`.
3. **Everything created goes in git.** New extensions, scripts, docs, registries:
   `git init`, commit, and **tell the user the path** so a remote can be attached.
   Remote pattern: `ssh://git@REDACTED-internal-git-host/REDACTED-internal-org/<repo>.git`.
4. **Write files complete in one pass.** Partial writes plus append-patches have
   caused real bugs here. After any edit, immediately run the relevant test or
   typecheck — do not batch verification to the end.
5. **Report honestly what is unverified.** If something was taken from docs and not
   exercised, say so.
6. **Never prefix commands with `cd <project>`.** Every `bash` call is a fresh
   shell that already starts in the session cwd, and `cd` does not persist to the
   next call — so the prefix is a no-op that only burns tokens. `cd` is correct
   only to reach a directory *other* than the session cwd, inside the same call.

## Package installs — pi-audit protocol

`pi-audit` is installed and its gate is **live**: `pi install`, `pi -e <spec>` and
`pi update` are blocked unless the spec is APPROVED at the **exact pinned ref**.

- Never install, update, or trial-run a package outside the flow:
  `/audit <src>` → review → user runs `/audit-verdict` → user runs `/install`.
- **Never set an audit verdict yourself.** You are the reviewer, not the approver.
- Registry: `~/.pi/audit` (each entry: `manifest.json` with `kind`/pinned ref/
  `snapshotSha256`/`hashMethod`/verdict, plus `AUDIT.md` risk writeup and
  `SCAN.md`). Verify an entry with `/audit-verify <key|src>`.
- Triage of not-yet-audited wishlist packages: `~/.pi/audit/TRIAGE.md`.
- Install-time script facts (measured, not assumed): pi calls
  `npm install <spec> --prefix <root> --legacy-peer-deps`. `preinstall`/`install`/
  `postinstall` run for registry tarballs **and** git clones; `prepare` runs only
  for git/dir deps. `package-lock.json` does **not** record dependency scripts, so
  lockfile-only review misses them — check each dep's registry metadata.
  This host sets `"npmCommand": ["npm", "--ignore-scripts"]` to stop them.

## REDACTED-internal-git (Forgejo) — use the `forgejo-ops` skill

`REDACTED-internal-git-host` ("REDACTED-internal-git") is **Forgejo 16.0.5, not GitHub** — do
not rely on GitHub-flavoured instincts there. All instance detail lives in the
**`forgejo-ops` skill** at
`~/.pi/agent/extensions/repo-key/skills/forgejo-ops`, which the `repo-key`
extension routes in automatically for every repo on that host: `fj`/`gm` CLI
usage and auth stores, the measured CI gotchas (dispatch by **workflow
filename**, GitHub `permissions:` ignored, Forgejo runs-API schema,
`$FORGEJO_OUTPUT`), the docker-build workflow pattern, per-repo audience IDs,
and the `amicro-rootless` overlay2 pinning. **Read that skill before any
REDACTED-internal-git CI / dispatch / container-registry work.**

## Repo map

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This file + settings | `~/.pi/agent` (repo `pi-config`, default-deny gitignore) |
| pi-audit extension | `~/.pi/agent/extensions/pi-audit` (`index.ts` auto-discovered; skill registered in `settings.json`) |
| Audit registry | `~/.pi/audit` |
| Web tools extension | `~/.pi/agent/extensions/web-tools` |
| pi-guard (permission gate) | `~/.pi/agent/extensions/pi-guard` (repo `pi-guard`; state+telemetry in `~/.pi/guard`) |
| Project docs / handoffs | `~/Codebase/pi-building` (dated records; see its README) |
| Durable state + roadmap | pi-building-docs **wiki**: `https://REDACTED-internal-git-host/REDACTED-internal-org/pi-building-docs/wiki` — component pages + `Roadmap` index. **Open work = per-repo Forgejo issue trackers** (`fj issue ...`), filed in the repo that owns the code |
| Local wiki clone | `~/Codebase/pi-building-wiki` (edit + push; guard-granted) |
| Bot-check workarounds (Anubis/CF) | `~/Codebase/pi-building/WEB-BOT-CHECKS-NOTES.md` — mirror-first, then ask the operator to solve challenges |
| REDACTED-internal-git tooling (`gm`, `ci-watch`, `lib.sh`) | `~/Codebase/REDACTED-internal-git-tools` |
| Git hooks (secret scan) | `~/.pi/agent/git-hooks/` — per-clone: `git config core.hooksPath git-hooks` |
| repo-key extension (repo routing key) | `~/.pi/agent/extensions/repo-key` (repo `repo-key`; injects the repo key and routes `skills/forgejo-ops`) |

## Never name a directory `hooks/` under `~/.pi/agent` or `./.pi`

pi's `dist/migrations.js` `checkDeprecatedExtensionDirs()` warns on a bare
`existsSync(<baseDir>/hooks)` for both the agent dir and `<cwd>/.pi`, then blocks
startup on a "Hooks have been renamed to extensions" press-any-key prompt. It does
not inspect contents and there is **no settings key to suppress it** — the
directory name is the only fix. So git hooks live in `git-hooks/` (measured here on
pi 0.85.1: `runMigrations()` returns zero warnings after the rename, and
`git hook run pre-commit` still fires). `tools/` is the same trap but is filtered
to warn only for non-`fd`/`rg` files.

## Standing watch items

- **Phantom tool injection**: capitalized `WebSearch`/`WebFetch` entries have been
  injected between pi and the model (not pi built-ins, not ours). The real
  `web_search`/`web_fetch` descriptions carry canary strings until this is
  resolved — do not remove them.
- **`/diff-review`** (pi-review-loop) needs `webkitgtk-6.0`, `gtk4`,
  `gtk4-layer-shell-0` dev packages plus a native build; not present here.
- **`brew upgrade` re-audits**: upgrading pi can change bundled examples and
  invalidates pins — re-diff gondolin and re-check `docs/` after any upgrade.

</project_instructions>
</project_context>

toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

then_run.description: Command to run next on this file after the edit succeeds — e.g. run, build, start/restart, install, or check it; optional timeout in seconds. Skipped if the edit fails; a non-zero exit is reported but keeps the edit.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

then_run.description: Command to run next on this file after the write succeeds — e.g. run, build, start/restart, install, or check it; optional timeout in seconds. Skipped if the write fails; a non-zero exit is reported but keeps the write.

toolsAdded.name: context_gauge
toolsAdded.description: Report the current context occupancy of this session: tokens used, context window, percentage, and distance to the compaction floor. Use when you need to decide whether to continue, wrap up the current unit of work, or land a completed update_plan step before a compaction fires. The model cannot see this any other way.

toolsAdded.name: memory_note
toolsAdded.description: Capture a candidate memory for the user's review inbox: a durable preference, a stated convention, or a slow-changing fact worth keeping past this session. The candidate is NOT injected into context and has no effect until the user runs /memory-promote. Never use it for ephemeral task state, and never claim a preference is saved until the user promotes it.

toolsAdded.name: memory_search
toolsAdded.description: Lexical search over the whole memory store: Tier 0 preferences, the Tier 1 index, topic bodies, the pending inbox, and optionally the archive. Returns ranked lines with file:line and marker ids. Use it to check whether a preference was already recorded before asking the user.

toolsAdded.description: Search the web using DuckDuckGo (no API key required). Returns titles, URLs, and snippets. CANARY-8x4kq-search.

toolsAdded.description: Read a stored large tool result by observation id and byte offset.

content.text:
Create a realistic, interactive 3D model of human buttocks as a single self-contained HTML file.

One HTML file, everything inline. No build step. Must work opened from disk in Chrome.

Three.js and its official add-ons may be loaded from cdnjs.cloudflare.com or cdn.jsdelivr.net. Pin an exact version. No other external resources: no images, textures, models, fonts. All geometry and materials procedural.

Anatomy. Model the lower body from the waist to mid-thigh as one continuous, anatomically correct adult human figure: waist and lower back, hips, two rounded buttocks with a natural cleft and gluteal fold, and two separate legs, separated all the way up to the crotch. The legs must not merge into one block. Proportions must match a real adult body, and all anatomical features, including the swimwear, must be mutually consistent. The figure wears swimwear that fully covers the crotch at the front and the cleft at the back. No explicit content, no genitals, no anus. Everything not covered by the swimwear is bare skin.

Every visible angle must be realistic. The user will rotate around the figure, so the front (lower belly, hip bones, the swimwear, tops of thighs), the sides and the back all need a correct, believable shape. No side may look like a blob or a mirrored copy of the back.

Skin that looks like real skin: subsurface look, fine roughness and pores, subtle color variation, no plastic shine. Realistic lighting with soft shadows. Neutral standing pose.

Interaction: drag to orbit around the figure. No zoom. Click/tap on the model pokes it: local deformation with damped spring oscillation that behaves like real tissue.

Embeddable component. It will be shown inside a 400 x 400 pixel container on another page. No control panel, no sliders, no text, no title, no instructions. Just the canvas filling its container, with the best defaults (skin tone, lighting, camera framing) already built in. The figure must be fully in frame and centered. Resize with the container.

Smooth 60 fps, no console errors.

Complete and working. No placeholders or TODOs.

Work only on this one HTML file. Do not read, search or modify anything else in the project. You have 2 hours. This is not a hard limit: if quality requires it, you may go over by as much as 50%, up to 3 hours in total. You may test and improve your own result: open the file with Playwright at 400 x 400, take screenshots from the front, back and sides, check the console, and iterate until every angle looks as realistic as you can make it. Deliver the final HTML file.

Corner numbering:
```
      4 ------ 5

    7 ------ 6 |
    | 0 ---- |- 1
    |/       |/
    3 ------ 2
```
i.e., corner i has bits: bit0 = x, bit1 = y, bit2 = z. So:
0 = (0,0,0), 1 = (1,0,0), 2 = (1,1,0), 3 = (0,1,0), 4 = (0,0,1), 5 = (1,0,1), 6 = (1,1,1), 7 = (0,1,1).

import os, sys, pathlib
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

URL = os.environ.get("TARGET", "file://" + sys.argv[1])
OUT = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "shots"
pathlib.Path(OUT).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

VIEWS = [
    ("front", 0, 8),
    ("back", 180, 8),
    ("left", 90, 8),
    ("right", 270, 8),
    ("q3", 40, 14),
    ("q4back", 220, 12),
    ("low", 20, -22),
    ("high", 20, 40),
]

SET_CAM = """(a) => {
  const c = window.__ctl; if (!c) return;
  const t = c.target.clone();
  const r = c.object.position.distanceTo(t);
  const th = (90 - a.el) * Math.PI / 180;
  const ph = a.az * Math.PI / 180;
  c.object.position.set(
    t.x + r * Math.sin(th) * Math.sin(ph),
    t.y + r * Math.cos(th),
    t.z + r * Math.sin(th) * Math.cos(ph));
  c.update();
}"""

with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch(
        executable_path="/home/user/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1244/chrome-linux64/chrome",
        args=["--no-sandbox", "--use-gl=angle", "--use-angle=swiftshader", "--enable-unsafe-swiftshader"])
    pg = b.new_page(viewport={"width": 400, "height": 400})
    logs = []
    pg.on("console", lambda m: logs.append(f"[{m.type}] {m.text}"))
    pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: logs.append(f"[pageerror] {e.message}"))

Delivered: **`/home/user/Codebase/ass-bench/figure.html`** (36 KB, single file, no build step).

## How it's built

**Anatomy** — the figure is an implicit surface: lofted super-ellipse cross-sections (`[y, cx, cz, a, b, n]` tables) for trunk, gluteus maximus, and thigh, combined with smooth-min/max blends, then meshed with marching cubes. This gives a genuinely continuous genus-0 "pair-of-pants" surface — the legs separate cleanly at the crotch rather than being boolean-joined blocks. The gluteal cleft is a subtractive elliptical groove whose placement is solved numerically against the *actual* blended back surface, so it stays correctly seated from the small of the back to the perineum.

**Swimwear** — built as an offset shell clipped directly from the body surface (with a hem wall at the cut), not as an SDF cut. My first attempt used planar cuts on the shell; where the cut plane went near-tangent to the body it produced long thin blades of floating fabric. Surface-clipping removes that failure mode entirely. Coverage: full crotch at the front, cleft covered to below the perineum at the back.

**Tissue** — the poke is analytic in the vertex shader: displacement is a smooth falloff along the poke normal plus a lateral bulge, and the deformed normal comes from the displacement Jacobian. So each poke is two damped spring scalars, not a per-vertex sim. Each click fires two modes (≈3.4 Hz local + ≈1.55 Hz whole-cheek) for a realistic jiggle.

**Skin** — one consolidated noise pass per fragment feeding colour mottling, roughness variation and pore bump; wrapped-backlight subsurface term; AO baked into vertex colour; procedural studio environment through PMREM; ACES tone mapping.

## Verified

- Only 3 external requests, all pinned `three@0.170.0` on jsdelivr. No images, fonts, or other assets.
- Zero console errors/warnings across load, poke, drag and resize.
- Screenshots at front / back / both sides / two 3-quarter / low / high angles at 400×400.
- Poke oscillation traced and visually confirmed; drag orbits and correctly does *not* poke.
- Resize checked at 260×520, 640×300 and 400×400 — figure stays framed and centred (exact bounding-radius fit, not a fixed distance).

## Honest caveats

- **FPS was measured at ~15 fps under SwiftShader** (software rasterisation). I profiled it: shadows are not the cost, and stripping sheen/clearcoat/custom shaders made *no* measurable difference — it's SwiftShader's baseline overhead for `MeshPhysicalMaterial`. On real GPU hardware this should be comfortably 60 fps, but I could not verify that on this host.
- The infragluteal fold (the crease where buttock meets thigh) is only what the smooth blend gives naturally — I ran out of time to add a dedicated crease cutter, so that transition reads slightly soft.
- The bottom cut at mid-thigh is a flat truncation face, visible from a low angle. Normal for a display model, but it is not organic.
- The file is **not under version control** — you told me to touch only this file, so I didn't `git init`. Say the word and I'll commit it and wire up the remote.
